meta.titre: Evidence for the Earth's Spherical Shape: proofs you can describe and rank
meta.sous_theme: Proofs of the earth's shape and how to present them in an answer
tags: evidence for the earth's spherical shape

sections.contenu_markdown: Stand on the beach at Limbe and watch a cargo ship sail towards the horizon. The hull disappears first and the upper parts stay in sight a little longer, as though the ship were sinking behind a hill of water. Everyday sights like this, together with eclipses and photographs from space, explain how people came to know the shape of the earth. The GCE asks you either to pick the most convincing proof in a multiple-choice question or to describe several proofs in your own words, and in both cases you must say how each one shows a curved surface.

items: A sphere is a round solid body whose surface is at the same distance from its centre at every point.
Light travels in straight lines, so an object hidden behind a bulge cannot be seen.
A lunar eclipse takes place when the earth lies between the sun and the moon.

sections.titre: Proofs that the earth is round
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The shape in one sentence

The earth is almost a **sphere**. It is very slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, but for GCE purposes we treat it as a sphere. Its circumference at the equator is about 40 000 km.

### The main proofs

| Evidence | What is observed | Why it shows a curved surface |
|---|---|---|
| Circumnavigation | Travellers who keep going in one direction (for example west) come back to their starting place from the opposite direction | The surface is closed and curves round on itself |
| Ship's visibility | A ship sailing away loses its hull first and its mast last; an approaching ship shows its mast first | The curve of the water hides the lower part before the upper part |
| Lunar eclipse | The earth's shadow on the moon always has a curved, round edge | Only a sphere casts a round shadow whatever its position |
| Circular horizon | The horizon looks like a circle from any open place, and a person who climbs higher sees farther | A curved surface makes the line of sight reach farther from height |
| Photographs from space | Satellites and astronauts photograph a round globe | A very large part of the earth is seen at once, with a curved edge |
| Pole Star | Travelling north, the Pole Star climbs higher in the sky; from far south it cannot be seen | The angle of view changes with the curve of the surface |

### Which is most convincing?

Circumnavigation is generally regarded as the strongest of the older proofs because the traveller actually goes all the way round the globe. Photographs taken by satellites show a very large part of the earth with its curved edge, but photographs taken from aircraft (aerial photographs) cover only a small area, so the curve is almost impossible to see in them. Day and night are **not** a proof of shape: they are a result of the earth's rotation.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks you to describe a number of evidences, with about two marks for each
variantes.contenu_markdown: For every proof write three short parts: the **name**, **what is seen** and **why this means the surface is curved**. For example: ship's visibility, the hull vanishes before the mast, so the sea surface curves between the observer and the ship. Do not write more than the number asked.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the same question also asks for the definition of the hydrological cycle
variantes.contenu_markdown: The hydrological cycle is the continuous circulation of water between the oceans, the atmosphere and the land. Water evaporates (and plants lose water by transpiration), the vapour condenses to form clouds, falls as precipitation, and returns to the sea by surface runoff and through the ground.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the 'most convincing' proof among four options
variantes.contenu_markdown: Remove options that cover only a small area (aerial photographs) or that need extra reasoning. Keep the option in which the observer meets the curved surface directly, and double-check that the option really concerns shape and not rotation.

sections.enonce_markdown: (a) Explain how the way a ship appears as it sails towards a port supports the idea that the earth is round. (b) Why is the earth's shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse evidence that the earth is a sphere? (c) Give one reason why satellite photographs are better evidence than aerial photographs. (6 marks)

etapes.justification: 'Explain' and 'why' need reasons, 'give one reason' needs a single reason.

etapes.action: Build the answer for (a): observation then reason.
etapes.justification: The observation alone earns half the marks, the reason about curved water earns the rest.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Mast first, hull later; the curved sea hides the hull.

etapes.action: Build the answer for (b): shadow, shape, sphere.
etapes.justification: You must link the round edge to a sphere and not just describe it.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The shadow is always curved; only a sphere makes a round shadow from every angle.

etapes.justification: A comparison needs a reason about area covered.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Satellites see a very large part of the earth, with its curved edge, at once; aircraft cover too small an area to show the curve.

etapes.action: Check each part has a reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: All three parts contain 'because' or a link word.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** As a ship approaches, its mast appears first and the hull later, because the curved surface of the sea hides the lower parts until the ship comes nearer. **(b)** During a lunar eclipse the earth's shadow always has a curved edge, and only a sphere throws a round shadow whatever its position. **(c)** Satellite photographs show a very large part of the earth with its curved edge, while aerial photographs cover a small area where the curve cannot be seen.

items.pourquoi_faux: It is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator.
items.correction_markdown: The earth is **almost** a sphere, slightly flattened at the poles.

items.erreur_markdown: "A ship disappears because it becomes too small to be seen."
items.pourquoi_faux: Distance alone would make the whole ship shrink and vanish at once. In fact the hull goes first while the mast remains visible.
items.correction_markdown: The hull disappears first because the **curved surface of the sea** hides it.

items.erreur_markdown: "In a lunar eclipse, the moon's shadow falls on the earth."
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes a solar eclipse. In a lunar eclipse the earth stands between the sun and the moon.
items.correction_markdown: In a lunar eclipse the **earth's shadow** falls on the moon, and its curved edge is the evidence.

items.erreur_markdown: "Day and night prove that the earth is round."
items.pourquoi_faux: Day and night are caused by rotation. They do not by themselves show the shape of the surface.
items.correction_markdown: Use evidence about shape: circumnavigation, ship's visibility, lunar eclipse, horizon or satellite photographs.

items.erreur_markdown: "Aerial photographs taken from an aeroplane are the best proof of the earth's shape."
items.pourquoi_faux: They cover a small area, so the surface seems flat.
items.correction_markdown: Only photographs taken from **space** show the curved edge of the globe.

items.enonce_markdown: Name **three** pieces of evidence that the earth is spherical.
items.solution_markdown: Any three of: **circumnavigation, ship's visibility (hull disappears first), lunar eclipse (round shadow), circular horizon, photographs from space, change in the height of the Pole Star.**

items.enonce_markdown: An aircraft flies at an average speed of 800 km/h along the equator, where the circumference of the earth is about 40 000 km. How long would one complete flight round the equator take without stopping? Explain why such a journey supports the view that the earth is a sphere.
items.solution_markdown:
Time = distance ÷ speed = 40 000 km ÷ 800 km/h = **50 hours**.

The aircraft goes on in the same direction and returns to its starting point from the opposite side without turning back, which is possible only if the surface is closed and curved.

items.enonce_markdown: A student writes: "Because the sun lights only one half of the earth at a time, day and night prove that the earth is round." Discuss this statement and give **two** better proofs, each with its explanation.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks as follows:

1. The statement is weak: day and night come from the earth's **rotation**, so they do not prove shape.
2. Proof one: **lunar eclipse**, the earth's shadow on the moon always has a curved edge, and only a sphere casts a round shadow from every position.
3. Proof two: **ship's visibility**, a departing ship loses its hull before its mast because the curved sea hides it.
4. (Alternative proofs: circumnavigation or photographs from space.)

**Answer: day and night show rotation, not shape; better proofs are the lunar eclipse and ship's visibility.**

items_markdown: The earth is almost a sphere, slightly flattened at the poles; its circumference at the equator is about 40 000 km.
Main proofs: circumnavigation, ship's visibility, lunar eclipse, circular horizon, photographs from space and the changing height of the Pole Star.
A good description gives the evidence, what is seen and why this shows a curved surface.
Circumnavigation is generally regarded as the strongest older proof; aerial photographs cover too little area.
Day and night result from rotation and do not prove shape.
The hydrological cycle is the continuous circulation of water between the oceans, the atmosphere and the land.
